dataset.name: Supporting data for "Frozen flume experiments indicate rapid permafrost riverbank erosion depends on bank roughness"
description: This dataset contains supporting files detailing five frozen flume experiments conducted at the Caltech Earth Surface Dynamics Laboratory to investigate rates of ablation-limited permafrost riverbank erosion under controlled conditions. Water flowed past a bank of saturated, frozen sand and ice and gradually eroded the bank by thawing pore ice and immediately entraining sand and washing it downstream. Experiments were scaled for flow hydraulics and heat transfer allowing comparisons between our results and natural permafrost riverbanks. For each experiment, we measured the initial and final sand bank topography using a Keyence laser scanner, water surface slope at 3-min intervals throughout the experiment using a Massa sonar scanner, bank erosion using 10-sec overhead timelapse imagery taken by an overhead camera, water and bank temperature using thermistors frozen into the sand bank and sampling at 2 Hz, and water discharge using an in-line flow meter. We include calibration data for the carriage (engineered by the Saint Anthony Falls Laboratory) used to make sonar and laser topography measurements. We also include calibration data for temperature sensors, water discharge measurements, and images of a regular grid placed in the flume to align overhead camera images with the carriage datum. Grain size analysis for the channel bed (gravel) was produced using a pebble count and bank sand was measured using a Camsizer X2. In addition to the five frozen experiments, we include sonar scans of water surface slope and Keyence scans of bed and bank topography for calibration experiments ran with an immobile gravel bank and bed.

measurementTechnique:
Methods are fully described in "Frozen flume experiments indicate rapid permafrost riverbank erosion depends on bank roughness" submitted to JGR: Earth Surface.
In summary, the experiments were run with one fixed wall and one erodible bank to compare measured erosion rates with theory for permafrost thaw by river flow. Experiments were conducted in the Caltech Earth Surface Dynamics Laboratory, in a 0.75 m wide and 7.60 m long flume that ended in a reservoir filled with chilled water. Experiments were run at bankfull with an initial width of 0.10 m and depth of 0.056 m. During the experiment, the bank eroded the channel to a width of 0.3 m and water discharges were manually increased to maintain bankfull flows.
Water and bank temperatures were cooled using a Mokon AL Iceman chiller that recirculated a 30% mixture of glycol in water through flexible pipes and mats. These were arranged to cool the end tank and freeze the sand-ice mixture in the test section. Air temperature was variable because the lab is not climate-controlled. The channel bed and upstream and downstream sections of the bank were constructed of gravel with grain size measured by Wolman pebble count. The frozen sandy test section had bulk density and ice content measured after each experiment, and sand grain size measured using a Camsizer X2 with the X-Fall accessory. We layered temperature sensors (Minco S667PFZ40BC resistance temperature detectors (RTDs) with ±0.2⁰C resolution) at known locations in the bank material before freezing the bank. Prior to the experiments, the temperature sensors were calibrated by submergence in an ice water bath at 0⁰C for multiple hours. Sensors were installed in three arrays (upstream (x = 2.5 cm), middle (x = 22.5 cm), and downstream (x = 42.5)) extending perpendicular to the channel with one protruding into the channel to measure water temperature at each array. Channel geometry and volume of bulk density samples was measured using 1x1 mm gridded laser elevation scans with a vertical accuracy of ~10 microns before and after sampling.
Water discharge was recorded every 10-sec using a flowmeter in line with the PVC pipe and controlled manually during each experiment using a variable frequency drive. We calibrated the water discharge by taking the mean time required to fill a 5-gal bucket (n = 4 to 6) at 4 different discharges.
Channel width and erosion rates were measured from overhead photographs (Nikon D750, 300 dpi resolution) taken every 10 sec using DigiCamControl. The water was dyed blue to enhance the contrast between the flowing water and eroding bank. Images were corrected for distortion using grids surveyed in with the cart to ~0.1 mm precision using Adobe Photoshop CS4 and thresholded to measure erosion rates (change in bank area through time) using the Matlab v2020a image processing package.
